---
title: "Checking sRtr on your own SAFs"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = FALSE
)
```

sRtr's automatic tests run on made-up data, because SRTR files cannot be
shared. Real files differ from release to release: columns come and go,
codes appear that no format lists, and identifiers that should match
sometimes do not. Before you rely on sRtr for an analysis, run the checks
below on your own standard analysis files (SAFs). They take a few minutes
and tell you whether sRtr behaves on your release as it does on the
releases it has been checked against.

The code is not run on this website, because it needs real SAFs. It uses
liver files; change the file keys for other organs.

# Share counts only

Everything below prints counts, never rows. Keep it that way if you change
the code, so you can share the results, for example in a GitHub issue,
without breaking the SRTR data use agreement. Mask any count from 1 to 10.
Masking each number is not enough on its own. If you share a total next to
masked parts, or two counts that differ by a few, a reader can subtract to
recover a small count.

```{r setup}
library(sRtr)
library(dplyr)

wd <- "path/to/your/SAFs"
set_srtr_wd(wd, release = "2303") # your release, named by year and month

mask_n <- function(n) {
  noquote(ifelse(n > 0 & n < 11, "<11", format(n, big.mark = ",")))
}
mask <- function(x) mask_n(table(x, useNA = "ifany"))
```

# 1. Run the package's live tests

sRtr's test suite includes live tests that run only on real files. They
check, among other things, that columns load with the right types, that
codes match the dictionary, and that derived outcomes are consistent. The
tests are not installed with the package, so you need a copy of the
source that matches the version you have installed:

```{r}
# The commit your installed copy was built from, if installed from GitHub:
packageDescription("sRtr")$RemoteSha
```

Clone the repository and check out that commit (in a terminal:
`git clone https://github.com/VagishHemmige/sRtr`, then
`git checkout <commit>`). Then, in a fresh R session:

```{r}
Sys.setenv(
  SRTR_LIVE_TESTS = "true",
  SRTR_WD = wd,
  SRTR_RELEASE = "2303"
)
testthat::test_local(
  "path/to/the/sRtr/clone",
  reporter = "summary",
  stop_on_failure = FALSE
)
```

Each live test names the files it needs and skips when your folder does
not have them, so you can run the whole suite with whatever files you
have. To run one area, add `filter`, such as `filter = "add_txf_outcomes"`.
A failure means sRtr does something on your release that it has not been
checked for. Please report it (see the end of this article).

# 2. Load with the warnings counted, not hidden

Loading a real file can give several warnings. Every sRtr warning has a
class, so you can collect each kind instead of hiding them all with
`suppressWarnings()`:

```{r}
seen <- list()
collect <- function(expr) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    expr,
    sRtr_warning = function(w) {
      kind <- class(w)[1]
      seen[[kind]] <<- c(seen[[kind]], conditionMessage(w))
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  )
}

tx <- collect(load_srtr_file("TX_LI"))
txf <- collect(load_srtr_file("TXF_LI"))

mask_n(lengths(seen))
```

The kinds you are most likely to see:

- `sRtr_warning_missing_columns` or `sRtr_warning_extra_columns`: the file
  does not have the columns the dictionary lists for this release. A long
  list usually means the release is wrong (check `set_srtr_wd(release =)`);
  a short one may be a real difference worth reporting.
- `sRtr_warning_unknown_codes`: values no format lists. sRtr keeps them as
  their own level, named `<code>: not in format`, and says which variable
  they are in. Some are known gaps in SRTR's dictionary; a new one is
  worth reporting.
- `sRtr_warning_dictionary_gap`: your release falls between the
  dictionary versions sRtr stores, and an entry differs between them.

To silence one kind in later code while keeping the others visible, muffle
only that class, such as `sRtr_warning_unknown_codes`.

# 3. Check the keys

Joins between SAF files rely on identifiers. These should hold, and
anything else is worth knowing before you join:

```{r}
mask_n(c(
  registrations = n_distinct(tx$TRR_ID),
  rows_beyond_one_per_registration = nrow(tx) - n_distinct(tx$TRR_ID),
  registrations_of_people_transplanted_again =
    n_distinct(tx$TRR_ID) - n_distinct(tx$PERS_ID),
  follow_up_ids_not_in_tx = sum(!unique(txf$TRR_ID) %in% tx$TRR_ID),
  missing_trr_id = sum(is.na(tx$TRR_ID))
))
```

`rows_beyond_one_per_registration` should be 0: each row of a transplant
file is one registration. Some people are transplanted more than once, so
there are more registrations than people. Every follow-up form should
belong to a registration in the transplant file. Each difference is
printed on its own, masked, rather than as two totals.

For donors, a deceased donor file covers only deceased donors, so some
transplant `DONOR_ID`s will not be in it:

```{r}
donors <- collect(load_srtr_file("DONOR_DECEASED", col_select = "DONOR_ID"))
mask_n(c(
  donor_ids_not_in_deceased_donors =
    sum(!is.na(tx$DONOR_ID) & !tx$DONOR_ID %in% donors$DONOR_ID)
))
```

# 4. Check labels

```{r}
unlabelled <- vapply(tx, \(x) is.null(attr(x, "label")), logical(1))
mask_n(c(columns = ncol(tx), without_a_label = sum(unlabelled)))
```

Almost every column should have a label, either the one stored in the SAS
file or one from the dictionary.

# 5. Check that derived outcomes add up

Derived variables should be consistent with each other. These checks use
the follow-up outcomes; the reasons behind them are in
[Follow-up forms are reports, not events](follow-up-forms.html) and
[Follow-up windows and death](follow-up-windows.html).

```{r}
tx <- add_txf_outcomes(tx)

# The status columns cover every registration once. Look at these tables
# yourself; shared beside the registration total, a table with a single
# masked cell gives that cell away.
mask(tx$FIRST_FU_MALIG_STATUS)
mask(tx$FIRST_FU_REJ_STATUS)

# The last negative form always comes before the first report.
gap <- tx$FIRST_FU_MALIG_DATE - tx$FIRST_FU_MALIG_LAST_NEG_DATE
mask_n(c(gaps = sum(!is.na(gap)), not_positive = sum(gap <= 0, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

`not_positive` should be 0. The merge report attached by
`add_txf_outcomes()` should agree with the status columns: registrations
with forms plus those with no follow-up make up all registrations. Check it
by computing the difference, which should be 0, rather than printing the
parts next to the total:

```{r}
report <- attr(tx, "txf_report")
report$registrations - report$registrations_with_forms -
  sum(tx$FIRST_FU_MALIG_STATUS == "no follow-up")
```

The time-to-event outcomes come from `add_time_to_event_outcomes()`, which
is not yet exported, so it is called with `sRtr:::`:

```{r}
out <- collect(sRtr:::add_time_to_event_outcomes(tx))

# No counted event falls after the end of follow-up or after death.
end <- pmin(out$TFL_LAFUDATE, out$REC_DEATH_DT_COMPOSITE, na.rm = TRUE)
counted <- out$FIRST_FU_MALIG_DATE_BINARY %in% 1L
mask_n(sum(out$FIRST_FU_MALIG_DATE[counted] > end[counted], na.rm = TRUE))
```

This should be 0.

# 6. Report what you find

If a live test fails, a check above gives an unexpected answer, or a
warning lists something new, please open an issue at
<https://github.com/VagishHemmige/sRtr/issues>. Include:

- the SAF release, and which files you used;
- `packageDescription("sRtr")$RemoteSha` and your R version;
- the check and its masked counts, or the warning's message (variable
  names and codes are fine; values from individual records are not).

Never attach SAF files or rows from them.
